how: Each attack runs the real Horos commands in a fresh directory against fake Airwallex, Airi and T:0; counts come from the fakes. Regenerate with `npm run demo`.

attacks.title: Supplier email moves the money
attacks.attack: After the payment is approved, an email claiming to be Slack asks for this and all future payments to go to a new IBAN.

attacks.title: The model is persuaded the email is routine
attacks.attack: The same email, but Claude's answer says ROUTINE and quotes a harmless line. The IBAN is still in the text.

attacks.title: Someone else already paid it
attacks.attack: While the passkey prompt is open, the bill is marked paid in T:0 by another system. Horos is not told.

attacks.title: The duplicate copy gets paid first
attacks.attack: A second accounting record of the same invoice appears, then is paid elsewhere, so it leaves the open list.

attacks.title: Authority expires mid-payment
attacks.attack: The last read of T:0 before confirming takes 20 minutes; the 15-minute mandate expires while Horos waits.

attacks.title: An operator retries a payment that went through
attacks.attack: The charge succeeds but its acknowledgement is lost. An operator tries to reopen the bill and pay it again with a second mandate.

result.said: not reopened: the provider does not prove this attempt unpaid; resolve PAID if it paid, or run reconcile when the provider is readable; second mandate: OBLIGATION_PAYMENT_UNKNOWN
result.note: the one charge is the original payment, which recovery then books as PAID

attacks.title: A mandate for a lookalike checkout
attacks.attack: The passkey-approved mandate points at the verified host, but another path on it.

attacks.title: An old approval after the destination changed
attacks.attack: A person re-verifies the bill to a different checkout. The earlier approval is then used to pay.
